relevance: The text is highly relevant to sports and exercise physiology as it investigates the impact of exercise and environmental conditions on immunological biomarkers in endurance athletes.
exercise_types: P1-HIIT: 2-hour high-intensity interval running in temperate conditions (23.4°C ambient temperature).
P2-EHS: 2-hour running at 60% ×O₂max in hot conditions (35.7°C ambient temperature).
P3-SS: 3-hour steady-state running at 60% ×O₂max in temperate conditions (23.1°C ambient temperature).

observed_effects.P1-HIIT: Plasma IgM, IgA, and IgG concentrations did not significantly change from pre- to post-exercise.
observed_effects.P2-EHS: Plasma IgA and IgG concentrations significantly increased from pre- to post-exercise. Plasma IgM did not significantly change.
observed_effects.P3-SS: Plasma IgM, IgA, and IgG concentrations did not significantly change from pre- to post-exercise.
observed_effects.Overall: Exertional-heat stress (P2) caused greater disturbances to plasma IgA and IgG compared to other protocols.

sex_differences: There was a significant difference between biological sexes in plasma IgA concentration in response to exercise (p<0.05), with a mean increase in female participants and a decrease in male participants.
evidence_strength: The observed changes were modest and remained within the normative range for a healthy population, suggesting a low-sensitivity response of EndoCAb to the exercise stressors. Effects were not clinically relevant.
